slides.headline: SME IPOs: The math behind the trap.
The Illusion of Easy Gains
slides.card_text: Retail investors often treat SME IPOs as lottery tickets, ignoring the asymmetric risk. While 21 multibaggers made headlines in 2026, the reality is a binary outcome. Investors frequently mistake speculative momentum for fundamental value, failing to realize that for every winner, there is a hidden cohort suffering 50% losses.

slides.headline: The Mechanism of Capital Extraction
slides.card_text: Risk is shifted to retail via aggressive valuation premiums. Institutional insiders often utilize the IPO window to offload positions, leaving retail holders to absorb the volatility. When the initial hype dissipates, the lack of fundamental support causes the stock to collapse, effectively transferring wealth from the public to early-stage promoters.

slides.headline: The Brutal Liquidity Trap
slides.card_text: SME platforms suffer from severe illiquidity and strict circuit filters. When sentiment shifts, retail investors find themselves trapped in lower circuits with zero buy depth. You cannot exit your position, meaning your capital is held hostage while institutional players have already liquidated their holdings during the initial surge.

slides.headline: Mathematical Compounding Drag
slides.card_text: A 50% loss requires a 100% gain just to break even. If your portfolio is heavily skewed toward speculative SME issues, one bad trade wipes out the gains of multiple winners. This volatility drag destroys long-term compounding, turning a 'multibagger' strategy into a net-negative wealth erosion machine over time.

slides.headline: The Non-Negotiable Institutional Rule
slides.card_text: Never allocate more than 2% of your total equity portfolio to SME IPOs. Furthermore, strictly avoid any issue lacking strong institutional (QIB) oversubscription. If the 'smart money' is not participating in the book-building process, you are likely the liquidity provider for those looking to exit.

slides.headline: The Pre-Trade Verification Audit
slides.card_text: Before allocating, run this 3-point audit: 1) Verify QIB oversubscription levels to ensure institutional interest. 2) Analyze the promoter's track record for past regulatory red flags. 3) Assess the free-float liquidity to ensure you can actually exit the position during a market correction. If it fails one, do not bid.
